खंड (2) अयोग्यता विवादों के लिए निर्णायक प्राधिकरण और प्रक्रिया को पूरी तरह राज्य विधान पर छोड़ता है, ठीक वैसे ही जैसे अनुच्छेद 243F(2) पंचायतों के लिए करता है।
exceptions_and_qualifications_hi: यह संरचना और सार में अनुच्छेद 243F के समान है, केवल 'पंचायत के सदस्य' के बजाय 'नगरपालिका के सदस्य' का उल्लेख करने में भिन्न है — अनुच्छेद 243F के तहत कोई भी व्याख्यात्मक सिद्धांत सीधे स्थानांतरित होता है।
अनुच्छेद 243F की तरह, राज्य-कानून-निर्दिष्ट अयोग्यता प्राधिकरण राज्य विधानमंडल के सदस्यों के लिए ही अनुच्छेद 192 की संवैधानिक रूप से निश्चित राज्यपाल-सह-निर्वाचन-आयोग तंत्र के विपरीत है।
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: अनुच्छेद 243V को अनुच्छेद 243F के शहरी प्रतिबिंब के रूप में पढ़ें — इक्कीस वर्ष की आयु-सीमा और राज्य-कानून विवाद-मंच डिज़ाइन याद रखने योग्य दो विशेषताएं हैं, दोनों पंचायत योजना से अपरिवर्तित रूप से आगे बढ़ाई गई हैं।

sections.title: Powers, authority and responsibilities of Municipalities, etc.
key_terms: State-law devolution of self-government powers to Municipalities
Twelfth Schedule as the illustrative subject-matter list for Municipal devolution

breakdown.plain_summary: Article 243W mirrors Article 243G's Panchayat devolution enabling provision for the urban context: State Legislatures may, by law, endow Municipalities (and, separately, the Article 243S Committees) with the powers and authority needed to function as genuine self-government institutions, including devolving economic-development/social-justice planning and scheme implementation drawn from the Twelfth Schedule's illustrative subject list.
essential_elements: The power is permissive ('may'), not mandatory — a State is not constitutionally compelled to devolve any specific power to its Municipalities.
Clause (a) covers Municipalities themselves, including plan preparation for economic development/social justice and scheme implementation.
Clause (a)(ii) cross-references the Twelfth Schedule as the illustrative area list for Municipal devolution.
Clause (b) separately empowers devolution to the Article 243S Committees (Wards Committees and others), also with Twelfth Schedule cross-reference.
exceptions_and_qualifications: This is the direct urban counterpart of Article 243G, sharing the identical 'illustrative, not authority-transferring' character — the Twelfth Schedule's eighteen entries (urban planning, land-use regulation, roads, water supply, public health, slum upgradation, urban poverty alleviation, fire services, etc.) do not by themselves confer legislative competence; actual devolution requires specific State legislation.

The separate treatment of Committees under clause (b) has no precise Part IX analogue, reflecting that Part IX's devolution clause (Article 243G) does not separately address sub-Panchayat committees the way Article 243W addresses Article 243S Wards Committees.
breakdown.how_to_read: Read Article 243W together with the Twelfth Schedule exactly as Article 243G is read together with the Eleventh Schedule — the Schedule supplies subject-matter examples, the Article supplies the enabling legal mechanism, and actual power transfer requires a third ingredient: specific State legislation.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: अनुच्छेद 243W, शहरी संदर्भ के लिए अनुच्छेद 243G के पंचायत अधिकार-हस्तांतरण सक्षम प्रावधान को प्रतिबिंबित करता है: राज्य विधानमंडल, कानून द्वारा, नगरपालिकाओं (और अलग से, अनुच्छेद 243S समितियों) को स्व-शासन की वास्तविक संस्थाओं के रूप में कार्य करने के लिए आवश्यक शक्तियां और प्राधिकार प्रदान कर सकते हैं, जिसमें बारहवीं अनुसूची की सूचक विषय-सूची से लिए गए आर्थिक-विकास/सामाजिक-न्याय योजना और योजना कार्यान्वयन का हस्तांतरण शामिल है।
essential_elements_hi: शक्ति अनुमेय है ('may'), अनिवार्य नहीं — कोई राज्य अपनी नगरपालिकाओं को कोई विशिष्ट शक्ति हस्तांतरित करने के लिए संवैधानिक रूप से बाध्य नहीं है।
खंड (क) स्वयं नगरपालिकाओं को कवर करता है, जिसमें आर्थिक विकास/सामाजिक न्याय हेतु योजना तैयार करना और योजना कार्यान्वयन शामिल है।
खंड (क)(ii) नगरपालिका हस्तांतरण के लिए सूचक क्षेत्र-सूची के रूप में बारहवीं अनुसूची का संदर्भ देता है।
खंड (ख) अलग से अनुच्छेद 243S समितियों (वार्ड समितियां और अन्य) को हस्तांतरण के लिए सशक्त बनाता है, जो बारहवीं अनुसूची संदर्भ के साथ भी है।
exceptions_and_qualifications_hi: यह अनुच्छेद 243G का प्रत्यक्ष शहरी समकक्ष है, जो समान 'सूचक, प्राधिकार-हस्तांतरणकारी नहीं' चरित्र साझा करता है — बारहवीं अनुसूची की अठारह प्रविष्टियां (शहरी योजना, भूमि-उपयोग विनियमन, सड़कें, जल आपूर्ति, सार्वजनिक स्वास्थ्य, मलिन बस्ती सुधार, शहरी गरीबी उन्मूलन, अग्निशमन सेवाएं, आदि) स्वयं विधायी क्षमता प्रदान नहीं करतीं; वास्तविक हस्तांतरण के लिए विशिष्ट राज्य विधान आवश्यक है।

खंड (ख) के तहत समितियों का पृथक उपचार पार्ट IX में इसका कोई सटीक समकक्ष नहीं रखता, यह दर्शाता है कि पार्ट IX का हस्तांतरण खंड (अनुच्छेद 243G) उप-पंचायत समितियों को उस तरह से अलग से संबोधित नहीं करता जैसे अनुच्छेद 243W अनुच्छेद 243S वार्ड समितियों को संबोधित करता है।
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: अनुच्छेद 243W को बारहवीं अनुसूची के साथ ठीक वैसे ही पढ़ें जैसे अनुच्छेद 243G को ग्यारहवीं अनुसूची के साथ पढ़ा जाता है — अनुसूची विषय-वस्तु के उदाहरण देती है, अनुच्छेद सक्षम करने वाला कानूनी तंत्र देता है, और वास्तविक शक्ति हस्तांतरण के लिए तीसरे घटक की आवश्यकता होती है: विशिष्ट राज्य विधान।

sections.title: Power to impose taxes by, and Funds of, the Municipalities
key_terms: Municipality's own tax/toll/fee levy authorisation power
State-collected tax assignment to Municipalities

breakdown.plain_summary: Article 243X reproduces Article 243H's Panchayat finance-enabling scheme for Municipalities: State law may authorise a Municipality's own-source taxation, assign State-collected levies to Municipalities, provide Consolidated-Fund grants-in-aid, and constitute dedicated Municipal Funds for crediting and withdrawing money — the complete four-part urban local-finance toolkit mirroring the rural one.
essential_elements: Clause (a) enables own-source Municipal taxation, subject to State-specified procedure and limits.
Clause (b) enables revenue-sharing via assignment of State-levied/collected taxes to Municipalities.
Clause (c) enables Consolidated Fund of the State grants-in-aid to Municipalities.
Clause (d) enables constitution of dedicated Municipal Funds for crediting and withdrawal of Municipal moneys.
exceptions_and_qualifications: This is textually parallel to Article 243H across all four sub-clauses, differing only in substituting 'Municipality/Municipalities' for 'Panchayat' — the same practical reality applies that grants-in-aid under clause (c) are typically the dominant revenue source given limited own-source taxation potential, especially for smaller Municipalities.

Larger Municipal Corporations (e.g., in major metropolitan cities) often have comparatively stronger own-source revenue bases (property tax, octroi/local body tax where retained, etc.) than most rural Panchayats, making clause (a) practically more significant for urban local bodies than its Article 243H(a) Panchayat counterpart.
breakdown.how_to_read: Read Article 243X as Article 243H's direct urban mirror — the four-part own-tax/assigned-tax/grants-in-aid/dedicated-Fund structure is identical, only the institutional beneficiary changes from Panchayat to Municipality.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: अनुच्छेद 243X, नगरपालिकाओं के लिए अनुच्छेद 243H की पंचायत वित्त-सक्षम योजना को दोहराता है: राज्य कानून किसी नगरपालिका के स्वयं-स्रोत कराधान को अधिकृत कर सकता है, राज्य-संग्रहित शुल्क नगरपालिकाओं को सौंप सकता है, संचित निधि से अनुदान-सहायता प्रदान कर सकता है, और धन जमा करने तथा निकालने के लिए समर्पित नगरपालिका निधियों का गठन कर सकता है — ग्रामीण उपकरण-समुच्चय को प्रतिबिंबित करने वाला संपूर्ण चार-भाग वाला शहरी स्थानीय-वित्त उपकरण-समुच्चय।
essential_elements_hi: खंड (क) राज्य-निर्दिष्ट प्रक्रिया और सीमाओं के अधीन, स्वयं-स्रोत नगरपालिका कराधान को सक्षम बनाता है।
खंड (ख) राज्य-उद्गृहीत/संग्रहित करों को नगरपालिकाओं को सौंपकर राजस्व-साझाकरण सक्षम बनाता है।
खंड (ग) नगरपालिकाओं को राज्य की संचित निधि से अनुदान-सहायता सक्षम बनाता है।
खंड (घ) नगरपालिका धन के जमा और निकासी के लिए समर्पित नगरपालिका निधियों के गठन को सक्षम बनाता है।
exceptions_and_qualifications_hi: यह चारों उप-खंडों में अनुच्छेद 243H के पाठ्य रूप से समानांतर है, केवल 'पंचायत' के स्थान पर 'नगरपालिका/नगरपालिकाओं' प्रतिस्थापित करने में भिन्न है — वही व्यावहारिक वास्तविकता लागू होती है कि सीमित स्वयं-स्रोत कराधान क्षमता को देखते हुए खंड (ग) के तहत अनुदान-सहायता आमतौर पर प्रमुख राजस्व स्रोत होती है, विशेष रूप से छोटी नगरपालिकाओं के लिए।

बड़े नगर निगमों (जैसे, प्रमुख महानगरीय शहरों में) में आमतौर पर अधिकांश ग्रामीण पंचायतों की तुलना में तुलनात्मक रूप से मजबूत स्वयं-स्रोत राजस्व आधार (संपत्ति कर, जहां बरकरार है वहां चुंगी/स्थानीय निकाय कर, आदि) होता है, जिससे खंड (क) शहरी स्थानीय निकायों के लिए अपने अनुच्छेद 243H(क) पंचायत समकक्ष की तुलना में व्यावहारिक रूप से अधिक महत्वपूर्ण हो जाता है।
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: अनुच्छेद 243X को अनुच्छेद 243H के प्रत्यक्ष शहरी प्रतिबिंब के रूप में पढ़ें — स्वयं-कर/सौंपा-गया-कर/अनुदान-सहायता/समर्पित-निधि संरचना समान है, केवल संस्थागत लाभार्थी पंचायत से नगरपालिका में बदल जाता है।

sections.title: Finance Commission (Municipalities)
key_terms: single Finance Commission reviewing both Panchayat and Municipal finances

breakdown.plain_summary: Article 243Y does not create a second Finance Commission — it extends the same Article 243-I State Finance Commission's mandate to also review Municipal finances and recommend on State-Municipality revenue distribution, tax assignment, and grants-in-aid, with the same mandatory laying-before-Legislature transparency obligation as Article 243I(4).
essential_elements: The Article 243-I Finance Commission is a single body reviewing both Panchayat (under 243-I) and Municipal (under 243Y) finances — there is no separate Municipal Finance Commission.

Clause (1)(a) mandates recommendations on State-Municipality revenue division, inter-Municipality-tier allocation, tax assignment, and grants-in-aid — mirroring Article 243I(1)(a)'s Panchayat-side mandate.
Clause (1)(b) additionally mandates recommendations on measures to improve Municipal financial position generally.
Clause (1)(c) allows the Governor to refer any other sound-finance matter to the Commission.
Clause (2) mandates the Governor lay every recommendation, with an action-taken explanatory memorandum, before the State Legislature.
exceptions_and_qualifications: The unification of the Panchayat and Municipal finance-review function in a single Article 243-I Commission (rather than two separate bodies) is a deliberate design choice ensuring a coherent, single view of the State's overall local-government finance picture across both rural and urban tiers.
As with Article 243I(4), the recommendations are not textually made binding on the State Government — only the laying-before-Legislature transparency obligation is mandatory.
breakdown.how_to_read: Read Article 243Y not as a standalone institution-creating provision but as a mandate-extension clause bolted onto the Article 243-I Commission — always read the two Articles together to get the complete picture of a State Finance Commission's full jurisdiction.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: अनुच्छेद 243Y एक दूसरा वित्त आयोग नहीं बनाता — यह उसी अनुच्छेद 243-I राज्य वित्त आयोग के जनादेश को नगरपालिका वित्त की भी समीक्षा करने तक विस्तारित करता है, और राज्य-नगरपालिका राजस्व वितरण, कर निर्धारण, तथा अनुदान-सहायता पर सिफारिश करने के लिए, अनुच्छेद 243I(4) के समान ही विधानमंडल के समक्ष रखे जाने के अनिवार्य पारदर्शिता दायित्व के साथ।
essential_elements_hi: अनुच्छेद 243-I वित्त आयोग एक ही निकाय है जो पंचायत (243-I के तहत) और नगरपालिका (243Y के तहत) दोनों वित्त की समीक्षा करता है — कोई अलग नगरपालिका वित्त आयोग नहीं है।
खंड (1)(क) राज्य-नगरपालिका राजस्व विभाजन, अंतर-नगरपालिका-स्तर आवंटन, कर निर्धारण, और अनुदान-सहायता पर सिफारिशें अनिवार्य करता है — अनुच्छेद 243I(1)(क) के पंचायत-पक्ष जनादेश को प्रतिबिंबित करते हुए।
खंड (1)(ख) अतिरिक्त रूप से नगरपालिका वित्तीय स्थिति में सुधार के सामान्य उपायों पर सिफारिशें अनिवार्य करता है।
खंड (1)(ग) राज्यपाल को किसी भी अन्य सुदृढ़-वित्त मामले को आयोग के पास भेजने की अनुमति देता है।
खंड (2) राज्यपाल को प्रत्येक सिफारिश, कार्रवाई-की-गई व्याख्यात्मक ज्ञापन सहित, राज्य विधानमंडल के समक्ष रखने के लिए अनिवार्य करता है।
exceptions_and_qualifications_hi: एकल अनुच्छेद 243-I आयोग में पंचायत और नगरपालिका वित्त-समीक्षा कार्य का एकीकरण (दो अलग निकायों के बजाय) एक जानबूझकर डिज़ाइन विकल्प है जो ग्रामीण और शहरी दोनों स्तरों में राज्य के समग्र स्थानीय-सरकारी वित्त चित्र का सुसंगत, एकल दृश्य सुनिश्चित करता है।
अनुच्छेद 243I(4) की तरह, सिफारिशों को पाठ्य रूप से राज्य सरकार पर बाध्यकारी नहीं बनाया गया है — केवल विधानमंडल के समक्ष रखे जाने का पारदर्शिता दायित्व अनिवार्य है।
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: अनुच्छेद 243Y को एक स्वतंत्र संस्था-निर्माण प्रावधान के रूप में नहीं, बल्कि अनुच्छेद 243-I आयोग से जुड़े एक जनादेश-विस्तार खंड के रूप में पढ़ें — राज्य वित्त आयोग के पूर्ण क्षेत्राधिकार की पूरी तस्वीर पाने के लिए हमेशा दोनों अनुच्छेदों को एक साथ पढ़ें।

sections.title: Audit of accounts of Municipalities
sections.raw_text: 243Z. Audit of accounts of Municipalities.—The Legislature of a State may, by law, make provisions with respect to the maintenance of accounts by the Municipalities and the auditing of such accounts.
key_terms: State-law Municipal account-maintenance and audit framework

breakdown.plain_summary: Article 243Z is the brief urban mirror of Article 243J — it leaves the entire framework for Municipal account-keeping and auditing to State legislation, without constitutionally designating any specific auditing authority.
essential_elements: The power is permissive State legislative competence, not a mandatory constitutional audit mechanism.
Both account-maintenance standards and the audit process itself are left to State law.
exceptions_and_qualifications: As with Article 243J, no constitutional counterpart to Article 148's entrenched Comptroller and Auditor-General is designated here — States commonly designate Directors of Local Fund Audit, examiners of local accounts, or similar State-created authorities by ordinary statute.
This is the shortest substantive Article across both Part IX and Part IXA, textually near-identical to Article 243J save for the Municipality/Panchayat substitution.
breakdown.how_to_read: Read Article 243Z as confirming that, just as with Panchayats, Municipal financial accountability runs through State-created audit machinery rather than any constitutionally fixed national auditor.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: अनुच्छेद 243Z अनुच्छेद 243J का संक्षिप्त शहरी प्रतिबिंब है — यह नगरपालिका खाता-रखरखाव और लेखा-परीक्षा के पूरे ढांचे को राज्य विधान पर छोड़ देता है, बिना किसी विशिष्ट लेखा-परीक्षा प्राधिकरण को संवैधानिक रूप से नामित किए।
essential_elements_hi: शक्ति अनुमेय राज्य विधायी क्षमता है, अनिवार्य संवैधानिक लेखा-परीक्षा तंत्र नहीं।
खाता-रखरखाव मानक और लेखा-परीक्षा प्रक्रिया दोनों ही राज्य कानून पर छोड़े गए हैं।
exceptions_and_qualifications_hi: अनुच्छेद 243J की तरह, यहां अनुच्छेद 148 के सुदृढ़ नियंत्रक एवं महालेखा परीक्षक के किसी संवैधानिक समकक्ष को नामित नहीं किया गया है — राज्य आमतौर पर साधारण विधि द्वारा स्थानीय निधि लेखा परीक्षा निदेशक, स्थानीय लेखा परीक्षक, या इसी तरह के राज्य-निर्मित प्राधिकरण नामित करते हैं।
यह पार्ट IX और पार्ट IXA दोनों में सबसे छोटा सारवान अनुच्छेद है, जो नगरपालिका/पंचायत प्रतिस्थापन को छोड़कर अनुच्छेद 243J के पाठ्य रूप से लगभग समान है।
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: अनुच्छेद 243Z को यह पुष्टि करने वाले रूप में पढ़ें कि, पंचायतों की तरह ही, नगरपालिका वित्तीय जवाबदेही किसी संवैधानिक रूप से निश्चित राष्ट्रीय लेखा परीक्षक के बजाय राज्य-निर्मित लेखा-परीक्षा तंत्र के माध्यम से चलती है।

sections.title: Elections to the Municipalities
sections.raw_text:
243ZA. Elections to the Municipalities.—(1) The superintendence, direction and control of the preparation of electoral rolls for, and the conduct of, all elections to the Municipalities shall be vested in the State Election Commission referred to in article 243K.
(2) Subject to the provisions of this Constitution, the Legislature of a State may, by law, make provision with respect to all matters relating to, or in connection with, elections to the Municipalities.
key_terms: shared State Election Commission for Municipal elections

breakdown.plain_summary: Article 243ZA does not create a second election-management body — it places Municipal elections under the same Article 243K State Election Commission that already administers Panchayat elections, and leaves the substantive law of Municipal elections to State legislation.
essential_elements: Clause (1) vests superintendence, direction, and control of Municipal electoral rolls and election conduct in the same Article 243K State Election Commission used for Panchayat elections.
Clause (2) leaves substantive Municipal election law to State legislation, subject to the Constitution.
exceptions_and_qualifications: This confirms the single-Commission design already implicit from Article 243K's drafting — one State Election Commissioner administers both rural (Panchayat) and urban (Municipal) local body elections in a State, rather than two separate bodies.
As with Article 243K, this Commission is entirely distinct from the Election Commission of India under Article 324, which has no role in Panchayat or Municipal elections.
breakdown.how_to_read: Read Article 243ZA as a short mandate-extension clause, exactly like Article 243Y's relationship to Article 243-I's Finance Commission — always read it together with Article 243K to see the complete picture of the State Election Commission's jurisdiction.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: अनुच्छेद 243ZA एक दूसरी निर्वाचन-प्रबंधन संस्था नहीं बनाता — यह नगरपालिका चुनावों को उसी अनुच्छेद 243K राज्य निर्वाचन आयोग के अधीन रखता है जो पहले से ही पंचायत चुनावों का प्रशासन करता है, और नगरपालिका चुनावों के सारभूत कानून को राज्य विधान पर छोड़ देता है।
essential_elements_hi: खंड (1) नगरपालिका मतदाता सूचियों की तैयारी और चुनाव संचालन के पर्यवेक्षण, निर्देशन, और नियंत्रण को उसी अनुच्छेद 243K राज्य निर्वाचन आयोग में निहित करता है जो पंचायत चुनावों के लिए उपयोग किया जाता है।
खंड (2) संविधान के अधीन, सारभूत नगरपालिका चुनाव कानून को राज्य विधान पर छोड़ता है।
exceptions_and_qualifications_hi: यह अनुच्छेद 243K के प्रारूपण से पहले से ही निहित एकल-आयोग डिज़ाइन की पुष्टि करता है — एक राज्य निर्वाचन आयुक्त किसी राज्य में ग्रामीण (पंचायत) और शहरी (नगरपालिका) दोनों स्थानीय निकाय चुनावों का प्रशासन करता है, न कि दो अलग निकाय।
अनुच्छेद 243K की तरह, यह आयोग अनुच्छेद 324 के तहत भारत निर्वाचन आयोग से पूरी तरह अलग है, जिसकी पंचायत या नगरपालिका चुनावों में कोई भूमिका नहीं है।
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: अनुच्छेद 243ZA को एक संक्षिप्त जनादेश-विस्तार खंड के रूप में पढ़ें, ठीक वैसे ही जैसे अनुच्छेद 243-I के वित्त आयोग से अनुच्छेद 243Y का संबंध है — राज्य निर्वाचन आयोग के क्षेत्राधिकार की पूरी तस्वीर देखने के लिए इसे हमेशा अनुच्छेद 243K के साथ पढ़ें।

sections.title: Application to Union territories (Municipalities)
sections.raw_text: 243ZB. Application to Union territories.—The provisions of this Part shall apply to the Union territories and shall, in their application to a Union territory, have effect as if the references to the Governor of a State were references to the Administrator of the Union territory appointed under article 239 and references to the Legislature or the Legislative Assembly of a State were references in relation to a Union territory having a Legislative Assembly, to that Legislative Assembly: Provided that the President may, by public notification, direct that the provisions of this Part shall apply to any Union territory or part thereof subject to such exceptions and modifications as he may specify in the notification.
key_terms: Union-territory extension of Part IXA with Governor-to-Administrator substitution

breakdown.plain_summary: Article 243ZB extends the entire Municipalities Part to Union territories using the identical Governor-to-Administrator, Legislature-to-Legislative-Assembly substitution formula that Article 243L uses for Part IX, again subject to Presidential tailoring by public notification.
essential_elements: 'Governor of a State' reads as 'Administrator of the Union territory appointed under article 239.'
'Legislature or Legislative Assembly of a State' reads as the Union territory's own Legislative Assembly, where one exists.
The proviso lets the President tailor the Part's application to a specific Union territory by public notification.
exceptions_and_qualifications: This is textually identical to Article 243L save for the Part IXA cross-reference, confirming the same drafting-economy technique was reused for the urban local-government Part.
breakdown.how_to_read: Read Article 243ZB as Article 243L's exact urban mirror — no substantive analysis differs between the two beyond which Part is being extended.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: अनुच्छेद 243ZB, अनुच्छेद 243L द्वारा पार्ट IX के लिए प्रयुक्त उसी राज्यपाल-से-प्रशासक, विधानमंडल-से-विधान सभा प्रतिस्थापन सूत्र का उपयोग करते हुए संपूर्ण नगरपालिका पार्ट को संघ राज्य क्षेत्रों तक विस्तारित करता है, फिर से सार्वजनिक अधिसूचना द्वारा राष्ट्रपति के अनुकूलन के अधीन।
essential_elements_hi: 'राज्य का राज्यपाल' को 'अनुच्छेद 239 के तहत नियुक्त संघ राज्य क्षेत्र के प्रशासक' के रूप में पढ़ा जाता है।
'राज्य का विधानमंडल या विधान सभा' को, जहां विधान सभा मौजूद है, संघ राज्य क्षेत्र की अपनी विधान सभा के रूप में पढ़ा जाता है।
परंतुक राष्ट्रपति को सार्वजनिक अधिसूचना द्वारा किसी विशिष्ट संघ राज्य क्षेत्र पर इस पार्ट के प्रयोग को अनुकूलित करने देता है।
exceptions_and_qualifications_hi: यह पार्ट IXA के संदर्भ को छोड़कर अनुच्छेद 243L के पाठ्य रूप से समान है, जो पुष्टि करता है कि शहरी स्थानीय-सरकार पार्ट के लिए वही प्रारूपण-मितव्ययिता तकनीक पुनः उपयोग की गई थी।
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: अनुच्छेद 243ZB को अनुच्छेद 243L के ठीक शहरी प्रतिबिंब के रूप में पढ़ें — कौन सा पार्ट विस्तारित किया जा रहा है, इसके अलावा दोनों के बीच कोई सारवान विश्लेषण भिन्न नहीं है।

sections.title: Part not to apply to certain areas (Municipalities)
sections.raw_text:
243ZC. Part not to apply to certain areas.—(1) Nothing in this Part shall apply to the Scheduled Areas referred to in clause (1), and the tribal areas referred to in clause (2) of article 244.
(2) Nothing in this Part shall be construed to affect the functions and powers of the Darjeeling Gorkha Hill Council constituted under any law for the time being in force for the hill areas of the district of Darjeeling in the State of West Bengal.
(3) Notwithstanding anything in this Constitution, Parliament may, by law, extend the provisions of this Part to the Scheduled Areas and the tribal areas referred to in clause (1) subject to such exceptions and modifications as may be specified in such law, and no such law shall be deemed to be an amendment of this Constitution for the purposes of article 368.
key_terms: Scheduled/tribal-area and Darjeeling Gorkha Hill Council carve-out from Part IXA

breakdown.plain_summary: Article 243ZC excludes Fifth Schedule Scheduled Areas and Sixth Schedule tribal areas from Part IXA by default, protects the Darjeeling Gorkha Hill Council's functions and powers from being affected by the Part, and gives Parliament the same PESA-style ordinary-law extension route Article 243M(4)(b) gives for Part IX.
essential_elements: Clause (1) excludes Fifth Schedule Scheduled Areas and Sixth Schedule tribal areas outright.
Clause (2) protects the Darjeeling Gorkha Hill Council's functions and powers from being affected by this Part.
Clause (3) lets Parliament extend the Part to Scheduled/tribal areas by ordinary law (not an Article 368 amendment) with tailored exceptions and modifications.
exceptions_and_qualifications: Article 243ZC is a noticeably shorter carve-out than Article 243M — it has no counterpart to Article 243M(2)'s exclusion of Nagaland/Meghalaya/Mizoram/Manipur hill areas, and no counterpart to the clause (4)(a) special-majority Assembly opt-in route, reflecting that those particular exclusions were specific to Panchayati Raj's rural character rather than to urban local government generally.

The Darjeeling protection here is framed slightly differently from Article 243M(3) — Article 243M(3)(a) excludes only the district-level Panchayat tier from Darjeeling, while Article 243ZC(2) protects the Hill Council's functions/powers generally without a tier-specific carve-out, since Part IXA's Municipality structure does not have a directly analogous district-level tier concept.
breakdown.how_to_read: Read Article 243ZC as a shorter, urban-tailored version of Article 243M — same Scheduled/tribal-area logic and same PESA-style Parliamentary extension route, but without the Northeast-hill-State-specific clauses that have no urban-local-government equivalent.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: अनुच्छेद 243ZC, पांचवीं अनुसूची अनुसूचित क्षेत्रों और छठी अनुसूची जनजातीय क्षेत्रों को डिफ़ॉल्ट रूप से पार्ट IXA से बाहर करता है, दार्जिलिंग गोरखा हिल काउंसिल के कार्यों और शक्तियों को इस पार्ट से अप्रभावित रखने की सुरक्षा देता है, और संसद को पार्ट IX के लिए अनुच्छेद 243M(4)(ख) द्वारा दिया गया वही PESA-शैली साधारण-कानून विस्तार मार्ग देता है।
essential_elements_hi: खंड (1) पांचवीं अनुसूची अनुसूचित क्षेत्रों और छठी अनुसूची जनजातीय क्षेत्रों को पूरी तरह बाहर करता है।
खंड (2) दार्जिलिंग गोरखा हिल काउंसिल के कार्यों और शक्तियों को इस पार्ट से अप्रभावित रहने की सुरक्षा देता है।
खंड (3) संसद को अनुसूचित/जनजातीय क्षेत्रों तक पार्ट को साधारण कानून द्वारा (अनुच्छेद 368 संशोधन नहीं) अनुकूलित अपवादों और परिवर्तनों के साथ विस्तारित करने देता है।
exceptions_and_qualifications_hi: अनुच्छेद 243ZC, अनुच्छेद 243M की तुलना में उल्लेखनीय रूप से छोटा अपवर्जन है — इसमें अनुच्छेद 243M(2) के नागालैंड/मेघालय/मिजोरम/मणिपुर पहाड़ी क्षेत्रों के अपवर्जन का कोई समकक्ष नहीं है, और खंड (4)(क) के विशेष-बहुमत विधान सभा ऑप्ट-इन मार्ग का कोई समकक्ष नहीं है, यह दर्शाता है कि वे विशेष अपवर्जन सामान्य शहरी स्थानीय सरकार के बजाय पंचायती राज के ग्रामीण चरित्र के लिए विशिष्ट थे।

यहां दार्जिलिंग सुरक्षा अनुच्छेद 243M(3) से थोड़ी भिन्न रूप से तैयार की गई है — अनुच्छेद 243M(3)(क) केवल दार्जिलिंग से जिला-स्तरीय पंचायत स्तर को बाहर करता है, जबकि अनुच्छेद 243ZC(2) बिना किसी स्तर-विशिष्ट अपवर्जन के सामान्य रूप से हिल काउंसिल के कार्यों/शक्तियों की सुरक्षा करता है, क्योंकि पार्ट IXA की नगरपालिका संरचना में सीधे समान जिला-स्तरीय स्तर की अवधारणा नहीं है।
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: अनुच्छेद 243ZC को अनुच्छेद 243M के एक छोटे, शहरी-अनुकूलित संस्करण के रूप में पढ़ें — वही अनुसूचित/जनजातीय-क्षेत्र तर्क और वही PESA-शैली संसदीय विस्तार मार्ग, लेकिन उन पूर्वोत्तर-पहाड़ी-राज्य-विशिष्ट खंडों के बिना जिनका कोई शहरी-स्थानीय-सरकार समकक्ष नहीं है।

sections.title: Committee for district planning
key_terms: mandatory District Planning Committee consolidating rural and urban plans
four-fifths rural/urban-elected-member composition floor for District Planning Committees

breakdown.plain_summary: Article 243ZD is the constitutional hinge connecting Part IX and Part IXA — it mandates a District Planning Committee in every State to consolidate the separate plans prepared by district Panchayats and Municipalities into one integrated district development plan, with at least four-fifths of the Committee's membership drawn proportionately from elected rural and urban local-body members, and forwards the resulting plan to the State Government.
essential_elements: Clause (1) mandates a District Planning Committee in every State at the district level, with the dual function of consolidating Panchayat/Municipality plans and preparing a whole-district development plan.

Clause (2)'s proviso fixes a hard floor: at least four-fifths of Committee members must be elected members of the district-level Panchayat and district Municipalities, apportioned by rural/urban population ratio.
Clause (2)(a),(c),(d) otherwise leave composition, assigned functions, and Chairperson-selection method to State law.

Clause (3) requires the Committee to have regard to spatial planning, shared natural resources, infrastructure integration, and available resources, and to consult Governor-specified institutions/organisations.
Clause (4) requires the Chairperson to forward the recommended plan to the State Government.
exceptions_and_qualifications: This is the first Article in either Part IX or Part IXA that operates across both Parts simultaneously — it is the structural bridge ensuring rural and urban local planning are not developed in silos within a single district.

The four-fifths elected-member floor is unusually high compared to most other composition rules in this Part, signalling a strong constitutional preference for genuinely local, elected-body-driven district planning over bureaucratic or nominated control.

Neither Article 243ZD nor Article 243ZE creates a body with binding decision-making power over Panchayats/Municipalities themselves — their output is a consolidated 'draft development plan' forwarded to the State Government, not a directly enforceable order.
breakdown.how_to_read: Read Article 243ZD as evidence that Parts IX and IXA, though textually separate, were designed as a single integrated decentralization scheme — the District Planning Committee is where the rural and urban tracks formally converge.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: अनुच्छेद 243ZD वह संवैधानिक कड़ी है जो पार्ट IX और पार्ट IXA को जोड़ती है — यह प्रत्येक राज्य में जिले की पंचायतों और नगरपालिकाओं द्वारा तैयार अलग-अलग योजनाओं को एक एकीकृत जिला विकास योजना में समेकित करने के लिए एक जिला योजना समिति अनिवार्य करता है, जिसकी कम से कम चार-पांचवें सदस्यता आनुपातिक रूप से निर्वाचित ग्रामीण और शहरी स्थानीय-निकाय सदस्यों से ली जाती है, और परिणामी योजना को राज्य सरकार को भेजा जाता है।
essential_elements_hi: खंड (1) प्रत्येक राज्य में जिला स्तर पर एक जिला योजना समिति अनिवार्य करता है, जिसका दोहरा कार्य है: पंचायत/नगरपालिका योजनाओं को समेकित करना और संपूर्ण-जिला विकास योजना तैयार करना।

खंड (2) का परंतुक एक कठोर न्यूनतम सीमा तय करता है: समिति के कम से कम चार-पांचवें सदस्य जिला-स्तरीय पंचायत और जिला नगरपालिकाओं के निर्वाचित सदस्य होने चाहिए, ग्रामीण/शहरी जनसंख्या अनुपात के अनुसार आवंटित।
खंड (2)(क),(ग),(घ) अन्यथा संरचना, सौंपे गए कार्यों, और अध्यक्ष-चयन पद्धति को राज्य कानून पर छोड़ते हैं।
खंड (3) समिति को स्थानिक योजना, साझा प्राकृतिक संसाधनों, अवसंरचना एकीकरण, और उपलब्ध संसाधनों पर ध्यान देने तथा राज्यपाल-निर्दिष्ट संस्थाओं/संगठनों से परामर्श करने की आवश्यकता रखता है।
खंड (4) अध्यक्ष को अनुशंसित योजना राज्य सरकार को भेजने की आवश्यकता रखता है।
exceptions_and_qualifications_hi: यह पार्ट IX या पार्ट IXA में पहला अनुच्छेद है जो दोनों पार्टों में एक साथ कार्य करता है — यह वह संरचनात्मक सेतु है जो सुनिश्चित करता है कि ग्रामीण और शहरी स्थानीय योजना एक ही जिले के भीतर अलग-थलग विकसित न हों।

चार-पांचवें निर्वाचित-सदस्य न्यूनतम सीमा इस पार्ट के अधिकांश अन्य संरचना नियमों की तुलना में असामान्य रूप से उच्च है, जो नौकरशाही या नामांकित नियंत्रण के बजाय वास्तव में स्थानीय, निर्वाचित-निकाय-संचालित जिला योजना के लिए एक मजबूत संवैधानिक प्राथमिकता का संकेत देता है।

न तो अनुच्छेद 243ZD और न ही अनुच्छेद 243ZE स्वयं पंचायतों/नगरपालिकाओं पर बाध्यकारी निर्णय-शक्ति वाला कोई निकाय बनाता है — उनका आउटपुट राज्य सरकार को भेजी गई एक समेकित 'मसौदा विकास योजना' है, न कि सीधे प्रवर्तनीय आदेश।
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: अनुच्छेद 243ZD को इस प्रमाण के रूप में पढ़ें कि पार्ट IX और IXA, पाठ्य रूप से अलग होते हुए भी, एक एकल एकीकृत विकेंद्रीकरण योजना के रूप में डिज़ाइन किए गए थे — जिला योजना समिति वह स्थान है जहां ग्रामीण और शहरी ट्रैक औपचारिक रूप से मिलते हैं।

sections.title: Committee for Metropolitan planning
key_terms: mandatory Metropolitan Planning Committee for ten-lakh-plus conurbations
two-thirds elected-member composition floor for Metropolitan Planning Committees

breakdown.plain_summary: Article 243ZE requires every Article 243P(c) Metropolitan area (ten-lakh-plus conurbations spanning multiple Municipalities/Panchayats) to have its own Metropolitan Planning Committee, with at least two-thirds elected membership proportionate to Municipal/Panchayat population, tasked with producing an integrated draft development plan that also factors in Union and State government investment priorities — reflecting that large metropolitan regions need planning coordination beyond what a single Municipality or district can provide.
essential_elements: Clause (1) mandates a Metropolitan Planning Committee in every Metropolitan area (as defined in Article 243P(c)) to prepare a whole-area draft development plan.

Clause (2)'s proviso fixes at least two-thirds elected membership, drawn from Municipality members and Panchayat Chairpersons in the Metropolitan area, proportionate to Municipal/Panchayat population ratio.

Clause (2)(c) uniquely allows representation of the Government of India itself on this Committee — no equivalent Union-Government representation appears in Article 243ZD's District Planning Committee scheme.

Clause (3) requires regard to existing Municipal/Panchayat plans, shared-resource coordination, Union/State objectives and priorities, and likely Union/State investment levels, plus consultation with Governor-specified institutions.
Clause (4) requires the Chairperson to forward the plan to the State Government.
exceptions_and_qualifications: The two-thirds elected-member floor here is lower than Article 243ZD's four-fifths floor for District Planning Committees — reflecting that Metropolitan Planning Committees are expected to also seat a meaningful share of non-elected institutional/expert/Union-Government representation given the scale and complexity of metropolitan-region planning.

The explicit Union-Government representation clause reflects the practical reality that metropolitan-region infrastructure (e.g., transport, water, environment) often involves Union agencies and Union-funded schemes, unlike ordinary district-level planning.

As with Article 243ZD, the Metropolitan Planning Committee's output is a non-binding draft development plan forwarded to the State Government, not an order enforceable directly against Municipalities or Panchayats.
breakdown.how_to_read: Read Article 243ZE alongside Article 243ZD as a matched pair — compare the different elected-member thresholds (two-thirds vs. four-fifths) and the Metropolitan Committee's additional Union-Government representation clause as the two clauses' main points of structural divergence.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: अनुच्छेद 243ZE प्रत्येक अनुच्छेद 243P(ग) महानगरीय क्षेत्र (दस-लाख-से-अधिक की बहु-नगरपालिका/पंचायत संयोजन) को अपनी स्वयं की महानगरीय योजना समिति रखने की आवश्यकता रखता है, जिसकी कम से कम दो-तिहाई सदस्यता नगरपालिका/पंचायत जनसंख्या के अनुपात में निर्वाचित है, जिसे एक एकीकृत मसौदा विकास योजना तैयार करने का कार्य सौंपा गया है जो संघ और राज्य सरकार की निवेश प्राथमिकताओं को भी ध्यान में रखती है — यह दर्शाता है कि बड़े महानगरीय क्षेत्रों को किसी एकल नगरपालिका या जिले की तुलना में अधिक योजना समन्वय की आवश्यकता है।
essential_elements_hi: खंड (1) प्रत्येक महानगरीय क्षेत्र में (अनुच्छेद 243P(ग) में परिभाषित) एक संपूर्ण-क्षेत्र मसौदा विकास योजना तैयार करने के लिए एक महानगरीय योजना समिति अनिवार्य करता है।
खंड (2) का परंतुक कम से कम दो-तिहाई निर्वाचित सदस्यता तय करता है, जो महानगरीय क्षेत्र में नगरपालिका सदस्यों और पंचायत अध्यक्षों से, नगरपालिका/पंचायत जनसंख्या अनुपात के अनुसार ली जाती है।
खंड (2)(ग) विशिष्ट रूप से इस समिति में भारत सरकार के स्वयं के प्रतिनिधित्व की अनुमति देता है — अनुच्छेद 243ZD की जिला योजना समिति योजना में ऐसा कोई समतुल्य संघ-सरकार प्रतिनिधित्व नहीं दिखता।

खंड (3) मौजूदा नगरपालिका/पंचायत योजनाओं, साझा-संसाधन समन्वय, संघ/राज्य उद्देश्यों और प्राथमिकताओं, और संभावित संघ/राज्य निवेश स्तरों पर ध्यान देने, साथ ही राज्यपाल-निर्दिष्ट संस्थाओं से परामर्श की आवश्यकता रखता है।
खंड (4) अध्यक्ष को योजना राज्य सरकार को भेजने की आवश्यकता रखता है।
exceptions_and_qualifications_hi: यहां दो-तिहाई निर्वाचित-सदस्य न्यूनतम सीमा जिला योजना समितियों के लिए अनुच्छेद 243ZD की चार-पांचवें सीमा से कम है — यह दर्शाता है कि महानगरीय योजना समितियों से महानगरीय-क्षेत्र योजना के पैमाने और जटिलता को देखते हुए गैर-निर्वाचित संस्थागत/विशेषज्ञ/संघ-सरकार प्रतिनिधित्व का सार्थक हिस्सा भी बिठाने की अपेक्षा की जाती है।

स्पष्ट संघ-सरकार प्रतिनिधित्व खंड इस व्यावहारिक वास्तविकता को दर्शाता है कि महानगरीय-क्षेत्र अवसंरचना (जैसे, परिवहन, जल, पर्यावरण) में अक्सर संघ एजेंसियां और संघ-वित्तपोषित योजनाएं शामिल होती हैं, सामान्य जिला-स्तरीय योजना के विपरीत।
अनुच्छेद 243ZD की तरह, महानगरीय योजना समिति का आउटपुट राज्य सरकार को भेजी गई एक गैर-बाध्यकारी मसौदा विकास योजना है, न कि नगरपालिकाओं या पंचायतों के विरुद्ध सीधे प्रवर्तनीय आदेश।
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: अनुच्छेद 243ZE को अनुच्छेद 243ZD के साथ एक मिलान जोड़ी के रूप में पढ़ें — विभिन्न निर्वाचित-सदस्य सीमाओं (दो-तिहाई बनाम चार-पांचवें) और महानगरीय समिति के अतिरिक्त संघ-सरकार प्रतिनिधित्व खंड की तुलना दोनों खंडों के संरचनात्मक विचलन के मुख्य बिंदुओं के रूप में करें।

sections.title: Continuance of existing laws and Municipalities
sections.raw_text: 243ZF. Continuance of existing laws and Municipalities.—Notwithstanding anything in this Part, any provision of any law relating to Municipalities in force in a State immediately before the commencement of the Constitution (Seventy-fourth Amendment) Act, 1992, which is inconsistent with the provisions of this Part, shall continue to be in force until amended or repealed by a competent Legislature or other competent authority or until the expiration of one year from such commencement, whichever is earlier: Provided that all the Municipalities existing immediately before such commencement shall continue till the expiration of their duration, unless sooner dissolved by a resolution passed to that effect by the Legislative Assembly of that State or, in the case of a State having a Legislative Council, by each House of the Legislature of that State.
key_terms: one-year transitional continuance of pre-1993 inconsistent Municipal laws

breakdown.plain_summary: Article 243ZF is the transitional savings clause for Part IXA, mirroring Article 243N for Part IX: pre-existing State Municipal laws inconsistent with the new scheme continue for up to one year after the Seventy-fourth Amendment's commencement, and already-sitting Municipalities continue for their existing term absent affirmative Legislative Assembly dissolution.
essential_elements: Inconsistent pre-commencement Municipal laws continue notwithstanding Part IXA, but only until the earlier of competent amendment/repeal or one year from the Seventy-fourth Amendment's commencement.
The proviso protects already-existing Municipalities' current terms, subject to early dissolution only via an affirmative Legislative Assembly resolution.
exceptions_and_qualifications: This is a now-largely-spent, purely historical transitional provision tied to the 1992-93 commencement, exactly like Article 243N — retained in the text as a record of the transition, with no ongoing operative significance today.
breakdown.how_to_read: Read Article 243ZF as Article 243N's exact urban mirror — no substantive analysis differs beyond which Amendment and which institution it references.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: अनुच्छेद 243ZF, पार्ट IX के लिए अनुच्छेद 243N को प्रतिबिंबित करते हुए, पार्ट IXA के लिए संक्रमणकालीन बचत खंड है: चौहत्तरवें संशोधन के प्रारंभ से असंगत पूर्व-विद्यमान राज्य नगरपालिका कानून संशोधन के बाद एक वर्ष तक जारी रहते हैं, और पहले से बैठी नगरपालिकाएं विधान सभा द्वारा सकारात्मक विघटन के अभाव में अपनी मौजूदा अवधि तक जारी रहती हैं।
essential_elements_hi: असंगत पूर्व-प्रारंभ नगरपालिका कानून पार्ट IXA के बावजूद जारी रहते हैं, लेकिन केवल सक्षम संशोधन/निरसन या चौहत्तरवें संशोधन के प्रारंभ से एक वर्ष, जो भी पहले हो, तक।
परंतुक पहले से विद्यमान नगरपालिकाओं की वर्तमान अवधि की सुरक्षा करता है, केवल विधान सभा के सकारात्मक प्रस्ताव के माध्यम से ही शीघ्र विघटन के अधीन।
exceptions_and_qualifications_hi: यह अब अधिकांशतः समाप्त, विशुद्ध रूप से ऐतिहासिक संक्रमणकालीन प्रावधान है जो 1992-93 के प्रारंभ से जुड़ा है, ठीक अनुच्छेद 243N की तरह — संक्रमण के अभिलेख के रूप में पाठ में बरकरार रखा गया है, आज किसी चालू प्रभावी महत्व के बिना।
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: अनुच्छेद 243ZF को अनुच्छेद 243N के ठीक शहरी प्रतिबिंब के रूप में पढ़ें — यह किस संशोधन और किस संस्था का संदर्भ देता है, इसके अलावा कोई सारवान विश्लेषण भिन्न नहीं है।

sections.title: Bar to interference by courts in electoral matters (Municipalities)
key_terms: delimitation-law judicial-review bar for Municipal elections
election-petition-only channel for challenging Municipal elections

breakdown.plain_summary: Article 243ZG closes Part IXA with the identical electoral-non-interference bar Article 243-O provides for Panchayats: Municipal delimitation/seat-allotment laws made under Article 243ZA cannot be questioned in any court, and Municipal election validity can only be challenged via a State-law-governed election petition.
essential_elements: Clause (a) is an absolute bar on questioning delimitation/seat-allotment law validity under Article 243ZA.
Clause (b) channels all Municipal election-validity challenges exclusively through an election petition mechanism under State-enacted procedure.
exceptions_and_qualifications: This is textually identical to Article 243-O save for the Article 243ZA cross-reference in place of Article 243K, and 'Municipality' in place of 'Panchayat' — the same Article 329 interpretive analogy applies with equal force here.
breakdown.how_to_read: Read Article 243ZG as Article 243-O's exact urban mirror, completing Part IXA's parallel structure with Part IX — with this Article, both the rural (Part IX) and urban (Part IXA) local self-government Parts of the Constitution are now fully captured.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: अनुच्छेद 243ZG पार्ट IXA को उसी निर्वाचन-हस्तक्षेप न रोक के साथ समाप्त करता है जो अनुच्छेद 243-O पंचायतों के लिए प्रदान करता है: अनुच्छेद 243ZA के तहत बनाए गए नगरपालिका सीमांकन/सीट-आवंटन कानूनों को किसी भी न्यायालय में प्रश्नगत नहीं किया जा सकता, और नगरपालिका चुनाव वैधता को केवल राज्य-कानून-शासित चुनाव याचिका के माध्यम से ही चुनौती दी जा सकती है।
essential_elements_hi: खंड (क), अनुच्छेद 243ZA के तहत सीमांकन/सीट-आवंटन कानून वैधता को प्रश्नगत करने पर पूर्ण प्रतिबंध है।
खंड (ख) सभी नगरपालिका चुनाव-वैधता चुनौतियों को राज्य-अधिनियमित प्रक्रिया के तहत विशेष रूप से एक चुनाव याचिका तंत्र के माध्यम से चैनल करता है।
exceptions_and_qualifications_hi: यह अनुच्छेद 243K के स्थान पर अनुच्छेद 243ZA के संदर्भ, और 'पंचायत' के स्थान पर 'नगरपालिका' को छोड़कर अनुच्छेद 243-O के पाठ्य रूप से समान है — वही अनुच्छेद 329 व्याख्यात्मक सादृश्य यहां समान बल से लागू होता है।
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: अनुच्छेद 243ZG को अनुच्छेद 243-O के ठीक शहरी प्रतिबिंब के रूप में पढ़ें, जो पार्ट IX के साथ पार्ट IXA की समानांतर संरचना को पूरा करता है — इस अनुच्छेद के साथ, संविधान के ग्रामीण (पार्ट IX) और शहरी (पार्ट IXA) दोनों स्थानीय स्व-शासन पार्ट अब पूरी तरह से समाहित हो गए हैं।

sections.title: Definitions (Part IXB — The Co-operative Societies)
key_terms: multi-State co-operative society definition
dual Central/State Registrar definition for co-operative societies

breakdown.plain_summary: Article 243ZH opens Part IXB (inserted by the Ninety-seventh Amendment Act, 2011, effective 15 February 2012) by defining its core vocabulary, most significantly distinguishing an ordinary State-registered 'co-operative society' from a 'multi-State co-operative society' (objects not confined to one State) and correspondingly defining 'Registrar' as either a Central Registrar (for multi-State societies) or a State-appointed Registrar (for ordinary societies) — the dual Union/State jurisdictional split that runs through this entire Part.
essential_elements: 'co-operative society' is any society registered (or deemed registered) under State co-operative-society law.
'multi-State co-operative society' is a society whose objects are not confined to one State, registered under law relating to such multi-State co-operatives.

'Registrar' bifurcates into a Central Registrar (multi-State societies) and a State-appointed Registrar (ordinary societies) — reflecting that this single Part governs both Union and State legislative competence over co-operatives.
'board' is the governing body, by whatever name called, entrusted with management direction and control.
'office bearer' is defined by an illustrative list (President, Vice-President, Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson, Secretary, Treasurer) plus any other board-elected person.
'State level co-operative society' is one whose area of operation extends to the whole State, as defined by State law.
exceptions_and_qualifications: This is the third and final self-government-institution Part inserted into the Constitution's local/associational-governance cluster (following Part IX's 1992 Panchayats and Part IXA's 1992 Municipalities), but co-operative societies are member-owned economic associations rather than units of political local self-government, making Part IXB's subject matter meaningfully different in character despite the parallel drafting structure.

The multi-State/State co-operative distinction reflects the underlying Entry 44 of List I (Union List, corporations other than co-operative societies... actually multi-State co-operative societies specifically) versus Entry 32 of List II (State List, co-operative societies) division of legislative competence under the Seventh Schedule — Part IXB does not itself allocate this competence but operates within that pre-existing division.
breakdown.how_to_read: Read Article 243ZH's Registrar/multi-State definitions as the key that unlocks the rest of Part IXB — nearly every subsequent Article's operative rule shifts depending on whether a co-operative society is an ordinary State-registered society or a multi-State co-operative society, as made explicit later by Article 243ZR's Parliament/Central-Act/Central-Government substitution rule.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: अनुच्छेद 243ZH, पार्ट IXB (सत्तानवेवां संशोधन अधिनियम, 2011 द्वारा डाला गया, 15 फरवरी 2012 से प्रभावी) को इसकी मूल शब्दावली को परिभाषित करके खोलता है, सबसे महत्वपूर्ण रूप से एक साधारण राज्य-पंजीकृत 'सहकारी समिति' को एक 'बहु-राज्य सहकारी समिति' (जिसके उद्देश्य एक राज्य तक सीमित नहीं हैं) से अलग करते हुए, और तदनुसार 'रजिस्ट्रार' को या तो केंद्रीय रजिस्ट्रार (बहु-राज्य समितियों के लिए) या राज्य-नियुक्त रजिस्ट्रार (साधारण समितियों के लिए) के रूप में परिभाषित करते हुए — यह दोहरा संघ/राज्य क्षेत्राधिकार विभाजन इस पूरे पार्ट में चलता है।
essential_elements_hi: 'सहकारी समिति' कोई भी ऐसी समिति है जो राज्य सहकारी-समिति कानून के तहत पंजीकृत (या पंजीकृत मानी गई) है।
'बहु-राज्य सहकारी समिति' वह समिति है जिसके उद्देश्य एक राज्य तक सीमित नहीं हैं, ऐसी बहु-राज्य सहकारी समितियों से संबंधित कानून के तहत पंजीकृत।

'रजिस्ट्रार' एक केंद्रीय रजिस्ट्रार (बहु-राज्य समितियां) और एक राज्य-नियुक्त रजिस्ट्रार (साधारण समितियां) में विभाजित होता है — यह दर्शाता है कि यह एकल पार्ट सहकारी समितियों पर संघ और राज्य दोनों विधायी क्षमता को नियंत्रित करता है।
'बोर्ड' शासी निकाय है, चाहे किसी भी नाम से बुलाया जाए, जिसे प्रबंधन दिशा और नियंत्रण सौंपा गया है।
'पदाधिकारी' को एक सूचक सूची (अध्यक्ष, उपाध्यक्ष, चेयरपर्सन, उप-चेयरपर्सन, सचिव, कोषाध्यक्ष) के साथ-साथ किसी अन्य बोर्ड-निर्वाचित व्यक्ति द्वारा परिभाषित किया गया है।
'राज्य स्तरीय सहकारी समिति' वह है जिसका परिचालन क्षेत्र संपूर्ण राज्य तक विस्तारित है, जैसा राज्य कानून द्वारा परिभाषित है।
exceptions_and_qualifications_hi: यह संविधान के स्थानीय/सहयोगी-शासन समूह (पार्ट IX के 1992 पंचायतों और पार्ट IXA के 1992 नगरपालिकाओं के बाद) में डाला गया तीसरा और अंतिम स्व-शासन-संस्था पार्ट है, लेकिन सहकारी समितियां राजनीतिक स्थानीय स्व-शासन की इकाइयों के बजाय सदस्य-स्वामित्व वाले आर्थिक संघ हैं, जो समानांतर प्रारूपण संरचना के बावजूद पार्ट IXB के विषय-वस्तु को चरित्र में सार्थक रूप से भिन्न बनाता है।

बहु-राज्य/राज्य सहकारी भेद सातवीं अनुसूची के तहत सूची I (संघ सूची) की प्रविष्टि 44 बनाम सूची II (राज्य सूची) की प्रविष्टि 32 (सहकारी समितियां) के अंतर्निहित विधायी क्षमता विभाजन को दर्शाता है — पार्ट IXB स्वयं यह क्षमता आवंटित नहीं करता बल्कि उस पूर्व-विद्यमान विभाजन के भीतर कार्य करता है।
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: अनुच्छेद 243ZH की रजिस्ट्रार/बहु-राज्य परिभाषाओं को पार्ट IXB के शेष भाग को अनलॉक करने वाली कुंजी के रूप में पढ़ें — लगभग हर बाद के अनुच्छेद का संचालन नियम इस पर निर्भर करता है कि कोई सहकारी समिति एक साधारण राज्य-पंजीकृत समिति है या एक बहु-राज्य सहकारी समिति, जैसा बाद में अनुच्छेद 243ZR के संसद/केंद्रीय-अधिनियम/केंद्र-सरकार प्रतिस्थापन नियम द्वारा स्पष्ट किया गया है।

sections.title: Incorporation of co-operative societies
sections.raw_text: 243ZI. Incorporation of co-operative societies.—Subject to the provisions of this Part, the Legislature of a State may, by law, make provisions with respect to the incorporation, regulation and winding up of co-operative societies based on the principles of voluntary formation, democratic member-control, member-economic participation and autonomous functioning.
key_terms: four co-operative principles constitutionally anchoring State incorporation law (voluntary formation, democratic member-control, member-economic participation, autonomous functioning)

breakdown.plain_summary: Article 243ZI grants State Legislatures the power to legislate on co-operative society incorporation, regulation, and winding up, but constitutionally anchors that legislative power to four internationally recognized co-operative principles — voluntary formation, democratic member-control, member-economic participation, and autonomous functioning — meaning State co-operative law must operate consistently with these principles rather than being entirely unconstrained.
essential_elements: The power is a State legislative competence ('Legislature of a State may, by law'), covering incorporation, regulation, and winding up.
That competence is expressly made 'subject to the provisions of this Part' — i.e., constrained by the rest of Part IXB's mandatory rules (board composition, elections, audit, etc.).

The four named principles (voluntary formation, democratic member-control, member-economic participation, autonomous functioning) are built directly into the constitutional text as the values State co-operative legislation must be based on.
exceptions_and_qualifications: This is the enabling foundation for the entire Part, comparable in structural role to Article 243B (Panchayats) and Article 243Q (Municipalities), but unlike those Articles it does not mandate any specific institutional tiers — co-operative societies remain voluntary member associations, not units of compulsory local government.

The stated principles mirror the internationally recognized Statement on the Co-operative Identity's core co-operative principles, reflecting that the Ninety-seventh Amendment was partly motivated by concerns over excessive government control and politicization of co-operative societies, aiming to constitutionally guarantee their autonomous, member-driven character.
breakdown.how_to_read: Read Article 243ZI as Part IXB's foundational values clause — every subsequent provision in this Part (board composition, election timing, supersession limits, audit requirements) should be understood as an attempt to operationalize these four principles, particularly democratic member-control and autonomous functioning.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: अनुच्छेद 243ZI राज्य विधानमंडलों को सहकारी समिति निगमन, विनियमन, और समापन पर कानून बनाने की शक्ति प्रदान करता है, लेकिन उस विधायी शक्ति को चार अंतरराष्ट्रीय रूप से मान्यता प्राप्त सहकारी सिद्धांतों — स्वैच्छिक गठन, लोकतांत्रिक सदस्य-नियंत्रण, सदस्य-आर्थिक भागीदारी, और स्वायत्त कार्यप्रणाली — से संवैधानिक रूप से जोड़ता है, जिसका अर्थ है कि राज्य सहकारी कानून को पूरी तरह अनियंत्रित होने के बजाय इन सिद्धांतों के अनुरूप संचालित होना चाहिए।
essential_elements_hi: शक्ति एक राज्य विधायी क्षमता है ('राज्य का विधानमंडल, कानून द्वारा'), जो निगमन, विनियमन, और समापन को कवर करती है।
वह क्षमता स्पष्ट रूप से 'इस पार्ट के प्रावधानों के अधीन' बनाई गई है — अर्थात, पार्ट IXB के शेष अनिवार्य नियमों (बोर्ड संरचना, चुनाव, लेखा-परीक्षा, आदि) द्वारा सीमित।

चार नामित सिद्धांत (स्वैच्छिक गठन, लोकतांत्रिक सदस्य-नियंत्रण, सदस्य-आर्थिक भागीदारी, स्वायत्त कार्यप्रणाली) सीधे संवैधानिक पाठ में उन मूल्यों के रूप में निर्मित हैं जिन पर राज्य सहकारी विधान आधारित होना चाहिए।
exceptions_and_qualifications_hi: यह संपूर्ण पार्ट के लिए सक्षम करने वाली नींव है, जो संरचनात्मक भूमिका में अनुच्छेद 243B (पंचायतें) और अनुच्छेद 243Q (नगरपालिकाएं) के समान है, लेकिन उन अनुच्छेदों के विपरीत यह किसी विशिष्ट संस्थागत स्तर को अनिवार्य नहीं करता — सहकारी समितियां स्वैच्छिक सदस्य संघ बनी रहती हैं, अनिवार्य स्थानीय सरकार की इकाइयां नहीं।

बताए गए सिद्धांत अंतरराष्ट्रीय रूप से मान्यता प्राप्त सहकारी पहचान वक्तव्य के मूल सहकारी सिद्धांतों को प्रतिबिंबित करते हैं, यह दर्शाते हुए कि सत्तानवेवां संशोधन आंशिक रूप से सहकारी समितियों पर अत्यधिक सरकारी नियंत्रण और राजनीतिकरण की चिंताओं से प्रेरित था, जिसका उद्देश्य उनके स्वायत्त, सदस्य-संचालित चरित्र की संवैधानिक गारंटी देना था।
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: अनुच्छेद 243ZI को पार्ट IXB के मूलभूत मूल्य खंड के रूप में पढ़ें — इस पार्ट में बाद का प्रत्येक प्रावधान (बोर्ड संरचना, चुनाव समय, अधिक्रमण सीमाएं, लेखा-परीक्षा आवश्यकताएं) इन चार सिद्धांतों, विशेष रूप से लोकतांत्रिक सदस्य-नियंत्रण और स्वायत्त कार्यप्रणाली को लागू करने के प्रयास के रूप में समझा जाना चाहिए।

sections.title: Number and term of members of board and its office bearers
sections.raw_text:
243ZJ. Number and term of members of board and its office bearers.—(1) The board shall consist of such number of directors as may be provided by the Legislature of a State, by law: Provided that the maximum number of directors of a co-operative society shall not exceed twenty-one: Provided further that the Legislature of a State shall, by law, provide for the reservation of one seat for the Scheduled Castes or the Scheduled Tribes and two seats for women on board of every co-operative society consisting of individuals as members and having members from such class of category of persons.
(2) The term of office of elected members of the board and its office bearers shall be five years from the date of election and the term of office bearers shall be conterminous with the term of the board: Provided that the board may fill a casual vacancy on the board by nomination out of the same class of members in respect of which the casual vacancy has arisen, if the term of office of the board is less than half of its original term.
(3) The Legislature of a State shall, by law, make provisions for co-option of persons to be members of the board having experience in the field of banking, management, finance or specialisation in any other field relating to the objects and activities undertaken by the co-operative society, as members of the board of such society: Provided that the number of such co-opted members shall not exceed two in addition to twenty-one directors specified in the first proviso to clause (1): Provided further that such co-opted members shall not have the right to vote in any election of the co-operative society in their capacity as such member or to be eligible to be elected as office bearers of the board: Provided also that the functional directors of a co-operative society shall also be the members of the board and such members shall be excluded for the purpose of counting the total number of directors specified in the first proviso to clause (1).
key_terms: twenty-one-director maximum board-size cap
mandatory SC/ST and women board-seat reservation on co-operative societies
five-year board term with casual-vacancy nomination-fill exception
non-voting co-opted expert directors on co-operative boards

breakdown.plain_summary: Article 243ZJ constitutionally fixes the ceiling and internal composition of a co-operative society's board — a hard twenty-one-director cap, mandatory reservation of one SC/ST seat and two women's seats where the society has members from those categories, a five-year board term (with a nomination-based casual-vacancy fill mechanism only in the term's second half), and up to two additional non-voting expert co-opted directors alongside functional directors who sit on the board without counting against the twenty-one-director cap.
essential_elements: Clause (1) leaves director count to State law but caps it at twenty-one directors maximum.
The second proviso to clause (1) mandates reservation of one SC/ST seat and two women's seats on boards of individual-membership societies with members from those categories.

Clause (2) fixes a five-year board term, office-bearer terms conterminous with the board's term, and permits casual-vacancy filling by nomination (from the same member class) only if less than half the original term remains.

Clause (3) mandates State-law provision for co-opting up to two additional expert directors (banking/management/finance/specialised fields), who are denied voting rights and ineligible for office-bearer election.
Functional directors are counted as board members but excluded from the twenty-one-director cap calculation.
exceptions_and_qualifications: The twenty-one-director cap and mandatory SC/ST/women reservation directly constrain State legislative discretion in a way that has no precise analogue in Part IX/IXA's more open-ended composition provisions — Part IXB is markedly more prescriptive and detailed about internal board mechanics than the Panchayat/Municipality Parts are about their own bodies.

The non-voting co-opted-expert-director design mirrors Article 243R(2)(a)(i)'s non-voting Municipal expert-member provision, again ensuring unelected specialists cannot outvote elected member-representatives — a recurring constitutional design pattern across all three self-government Parts.

The casual-vacancy nomination exception is itself a deliberate carve-out from the 'democratic member-control' principle of Article 243ZI, justified only for the practical case where so little of the term remains that a fresh election would be disproportionate.
breakdown.how_to_read: Read Article 243ZJ as the single most detailed internal-governance Article across Parts IX, IXA, and IXB — its numeric specificity (twenty-one directors, five years, two co-opted members, one SC/ST plus two women's seats) reflects Parliament's intent to directly constitutionalize co-operative board mechanics rather than leave them entirely to State discretion, a notably stronger intervention than the corresponding Panchayat/Municipality provisions.

sections.title: Election of members of board
sections.raw_text:
243ZK. Election of members of board.—(1) Notwithstanding anything contained in any law made by the Legislature of a State, the election of a board shall be conducted before the expiry of the term of the board so as to ensure that the newly elected members of the board assume office immediately on the expiry of the term of the office of members of the outgoing board.
(2) The superintendence, direction and control of the preparation of electoral rolls for, and the conduct of, all elections to a co-operative society shall vest in such an authority or body, as may be provided by the Legislature of a State, by law: Provided that the Legislature of a State may, by law, provide for the procedure and guidelines for the conduct of such elections.
key_terms: seamless board-transition election-timing mandate for co-operative societies
State-law-designated election authority for co-operative societies

breakdown.plain_summary: Article 243ZK mandates that co-operative board elections be conducted before the outgoing board's term expires, so the newly elected board can assume office immediately without any administrative gap, and leaves the identity of the election-conducting authority (unlike Article 243K's constitutionally fixed State Election Commission for Panchayats/Municipalities) entirely to State law.
essential_elements: Clause (1) mandates election completion before the outgoing board's term expires, ensuring immediate, gap-free handover — this overrides any contrary State law ('notwithstanding').
Clause (2) vests superintendence, direction, and control of co-operative electoral rolls and election conduct in whatever authority or body State law designates.
The proviso to clause (2) allows State law to further prescribe procedure and guidelines for conducting such elections.
exceptions_and_qualifications: This is a deliberate structural departure from both Article 243K (Panchayats) and Article 243ZA (Municipalities), which vest election administration in a single constitutionally created State Election Commission — Article 243ZK leaves the choice of election authority to ordinary State legislation, reflecting that co-operative societies are member-owned economic bodies rather than units of political government, so a less constitutionally rigid election-administration structure was considered appropriate.

The seamless-transition mandate directly serves the Article 243ZI 'democratic member-control' principle and the Article 243ZL six-month supersession cap by preventing administrative or political actors from indefinitely delaying board elections to prolong an outgoing board's (or an appointed administrator's) control.
breakdown.how_to_read: Read Article 243ZK's clause (1) timing mandate together with Article 243ZL's supersession cap — together they form the two-part guarantee against a co-operative society being left without a genuinely elected board for any extended period.

sections.title: Supersession and suspension of board and interim management
sections.raw_text:
243ZL. Supersession and suspension of board and interim management.—(1) Notwithstanding anything contained in any law for the time being in force, no board shall be superseded or kept under suspension for a period exceeding six months: Provided that the board may be superseded or kept under suspension in a case—
(i) of its persistent default; or
(ii) of negligence in the performance of its duties; or
(iii) the board has committed any act prejudicial to the interests of the co-operative society or its members; or
(iv) there is stalemate in the constitution or functions of the board; or
(v) the authority or body as provided by the Legislature of a State, by law, under clause (2) of article 243ZK, has failed to conduct elections in accordance with the provisions of the State Act: Provided further that the board of any such co-operative society shall not be superseded or kept under suspension where there is no Government shareholding or loan or financial assistance or any guarantee by the Government: Provided also that in case of a co-operative society carrying on the business of banking, the provisions of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 shall also apply: Provided also that in case of a co-operative society, other than a multi-State co-operative society, carrying on the business of banking, the provisions of this clause shall have the effect as if for the words “six months”, the words “one year” had been substituted.
(2) In case of supersession of a board, the administrator appointed to manage the affairs of such co-operative society shall arrange for conduct of elections within the period specified in clause (1) and handover the management to the elected board.
(3) The Legislature of a State may, by law, make provisions for the conditions of service of the administrator.
key_terms: six-month maximum board supersession/suspension cap
five enumerated statutory grounds for co-operative board supersession
no-Government-stake immunity from board supersession
one-year supersession cap for non-multi-State banking co-operatives

breakdown.plain_summary: Article 243ZL is Part IXB's centerpiece autonomy guarantee: a co-operative board cannot be superseded or suspended for more than six months (extended to one year for non-multi-State banking co-operatives), only on five enumerated grounds (persistent default, negligence, prejudicial acts, board stalemate, or election-conduct failure), never at all if the Government has no shareholding/loan/financial-assistance/guarantee stake in the society, and any appointed administrator during supersession must arrange fresh elections within the capped period and hand over to the newly elected board.
essential_elements: Clause (1) caps supersession/suspension at six months as an overriding rule ('notwithstanding anything contained in any law').

The first proviso limits permissible grounds to five enumerated categories: persistent default, negligence, prejudicial conduct, constitutional/functional stalemate, or election-conduct failure by the designated authority.

The second proviso creates a complete immunity from supersession/suspension where the Government has no shareholding, loan, financial assistance, or guarantee in the society — protecting genuinely independent co-operatives from any government takeover mechanism at all.
The third proviso layers in the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 for banking co-operatives, on top of (not instead of) this Article's rules.
The fourth proviso extends the cap to one year specifically for non-multi-State banking co-operatives (multi-State banking co-operatives remain at six months).
Clause (2) obliges the administrator to arrange elections within the capped period and hand over management to the newly elected board.
Clause (3) leaves the administrator's service conditions to State law.
exceptions_and_qualifications: This Article has no direct Part IX/IXA analogue — neither Panchayats nor Municipalities have anything resembling a 'supersession by administrator' concept in their core text, since their elected-body continuity is instead protected via Article 243E/243U's duration-and-reconstitution scheme; Part IXB instead directly confronts and constitutionally limits a real historical practice (government supersession of co-operative boards for political control) that was a specific driver of the Ninety-seventh Amendment.

The no-Government-stake immunity is a particularly strong autonomy protection, constitutionally foreclosing government supersession entirely for co-operatives that receive no government financial support — directly implementing the Article 243ZI 'autonomous functioning' principle.

The enumerated five grounds function similarly to the closed-list disqualification/dissolution grounds seen elsewhere in the Constitution, constraining executive discretion by confining supersession to specific, objectively assessable triggers rather than open-ended government satisfaction.
breakdown.how_to_read: Read Article 243ZL as Part IXB's answer to the historical problem of government-controlled 'administrator raj' over co-operative societies — the six-month/one-year caps, closed grounds list, and no-Government-stake immunity together operationalize the Article 243ZI autonomous-functioning principle with concrete, judicially enforceable numeric and categorical limits.

sections.title: Audit of accounts of co-operative societies
sections.raw_text:
243ZM. Audit of accounts of co-operative societies.—(1) The Legislature of a State may, by law, make provisions with respect to the maintenance of accounts by the co-operative societies and the auditing of such accounts at least once in each financial year.
(2) The Legislature of a State shall, by law, lay down the minimum qualifications and experience of auditors and auditing firms that shall be eligible for auditing accounts of the co-operative societies.
(3) Every co-operative society shall cause to be audited by an auditor or auditing firms referred to in clause (2) appointed by the general body of the co-operative society: Provided that such auditors or auditing firms shall be appointed from a panel approved by a State Government or an authority authorised by the State Government in this behalf.
(4) The accounts of every co-operative society shall be audited within six months of the close of the financial year to which such accounts relate.
(5) The audit report of the accounts of an apex co-operative society, as may be defined by the State Act, shall be laid before the State Legislature in the manner, as may be provided by the State Legislature, by law.
key_terms: mandatory annual audit with prescribed auditor qualifications and State-approved panel
six-month post-financial-year audit completion deadline for co-operative societies
apex co-operative society audit report laid before State Legislature

breakdown.plain_summary: Article 243ZM sets a far more prescriptive audit regime for co-operative societies than Article 243J/243Z do for Panchayats/Municipalities: annual auditing is required, State law must fix minimum auditor qualifications, auditors must be appointed by the general body itself (not management) from a State-approved panel, the audit must complete within six months of financial-year close, and an apex society's audit report must specifically be laid before the State Legislature.
essential_elements: Clause (1) empowers State law on account maintenance and mandates auditing at least once every financial year.
Clause (2) mandates (not merely permits) State law to fix minimum auditor/auditing-firm qualifications and experience.
Clause (3) requires the general body (the society's members collectively) — not the board — to appoint the auditor, from a State-Government-approved panel.
Clause (4) fixes a hard six-month deadline from financial-year close for audit completion.
Clause (5) mandates apex co-operative societies' audit reports be laid before the State Legislature, per State-law-specified manner.
exceptions_and_qualifications: This is markedly more detailed than Article 243J (Panchayat audit) and Article 243Z (Municipal audit), both of which are single-sentence permissive enabling clauses with no qualification standards, appointment-authority rule, deadline, or legislative-laying requirement — reflecting Part IXB's generally more prescriptive drafting style, consistent with co-operative societies' character as member-owned bodies handling members' own funds and requiring stronger independent financial-accountability safeguards.

Requiring the general body (rather than the board) to appoint the auditor is a direct implementation of the Article 243ZI democratic member-control principle, preventing board self-selection of a compliant auditor.

The apex-society laying-before-Legislature requirement parallels Article 243I(4)/243Y(2)'s Finance Commission report-laying obligations, extending similar public-accountability logic to large co-operative structures.
breakdown.how_to_read: Read Article 243ZM as Part IXB's financial-accountability core — contrast its detail (qualification standards, general-body appointment, fixed deadline) against the single-sentence brevity of Articles 243J and 243Z to appreciate how much more constitutionally prescriptive co-operative-society audit regulation is compared to Panchayat/Municipal audit regulation.

sections.title: Convening of general body meetings
sections.raw_text: 243ZN. Convening of general body meetings.—The Legislature of a State may, by law, make provisions that the annual general body meeting of every co-operative society shall be convened within a period of six months of close of the financial year to transact the business as may be provided in such law.
key_terms: six-month annual general body meeting deadline

breakdown.plain_summary: Article 243ZN empowers State law to require every co-operative society's annual general body meeting to be held within six months of financial-year close, ensuring the membership convenes regularly to transact the business State law specifies (typically including reviewing the audited accounts required under Article 243ZM).
essential_elements: The power is permissive State legislative competence, structured around a specific six-month timing benchmark.
The meeting's business content is left to State law.
exceptions_and_qualifications: This Article works hand-in-glove with Article 243ZM(4)'s six-month audit-completion deadline — the timing alignment is deliberate, since an annual general body meeting convened within six months of financial-year close can practically review the audited accounts completed within that same window.

There is no precise Part IX/IXA equivalent mandating a specific meeting cadence for Panchayats or Municipalities at the constitutional level (though State laws for those bodies typically prescribe their own meeting schedules by ordinary legislation).
breakdown.how_to_read: Read Article 243ZN together with Article 243ZM as a coordinated pair — the audit deadline and the annual general meeting deadline are both fixed at six months precisely so the audited accounts can be placed before the membership at that meeting.

sections.title: Right of a member to get information
sections.raw_text:
243ZO. Right of a member to get information.—(1) The Legislature of a State may, by law, provide for access to every member of a co-operative society to the books, information and accounts of the co-operative society kept in regular transaction of its business with such member.
(2) The Legislature of a State may, by law, make provisions to ensure the participation of members in the management of the co-operative society providing minimum requirement of attending meetings by the members and utilising the minimum level of services as may be provided in such law.
(3) The Legislature of a State may, by law, provide for co-operative education and training for its members.
key_terms: member's right of access to the co-operative society's own transaction records
minimum-participation requirement for co-operative society members

breakdown.plain_summary: Article 243ZO empowers State law to give every member a right to access the society's books, information, and accounts relating to that member's own regular transactions with the society, to impose minimum meeting-attendance and service-utilisation participation requirements on members, and to provide for co-operative education and training.
essential_elements: Clause (1) is member-transparency-focused: access is specifically to records of the society's regular transactions with that particular member, not necessarily the society's entire books at large.
Clause (2) is member-participation-focused: minimum attendance and minimum service-utilisation requirements can be imposed on members by State law.
Clause (3) empowers State law on co-operative education and training for members.
exceptions_and_qualifications: This trio of provisions directly operationalizes the Article 243ZI 'member-economic participation' and 'democratic member-control' principles by giving members both an information right (to hold the board accountable) and a reciprocal minimum-participation obligation (so membership carries genuine engagement, not passive nominal status).

The clause (1) access right is narrower than a general right to information over all society affairs — it is textually confined to records of the member's own regular transactions with the society, distinguishing it from a broader RTI-style transparency mandate.
breakdown.how_to_read: Read Article 243ZO as Part IXB's member-empowerment triad — information access, participation minimums, and education/training together aim to keep the co-operative genuinely member-driven rather than board- or bureaucracy-driven, consistent with the Article 243ZI foundational principles.

sections.title: Returns
key_terms: six-item mandatory annual return to State-designated authority

breakdown.plain_summary: Article 243ZP directly (not merely via enabling State legislation) imposes a mandatory annual filing obligation on every co-operative society: within six months of financial-year close, it must file a six-item return — activity report, audited accounts, general-body-approved surplus-disposal plan, bye-law amendments, a declaration on general-body-meeting/election timing, and any other Registrar-required information — with the State-Government-designated authority.
essential_elements: This is a directly operative constitutional mandate on co-operative societies themselves, not merely an enabling clause for State legislation — the obligation and its six-item content are fixed by the constitutional text itself.
The six-month deadline again aligns with the Article 243ZM audit deadline and the Article 243ZN annual general body meeting deadline.
Item (e)'s declaration on election-conduct timing functions as a self-reporting compliance check tying back to Article 243ZK's election-timing mandate.
Item (f) is an open-ended catch-all allowing the Registrar to require further information under State Act provisions.
exceptions_and_qualifications: Article 243ZP stands out within Part IXB (and across Parts IX/IXA/IXB generally) as one of the few provisions imposing a directly binding obligation on the regulated institution itself rather than merely empowering State legislation — most surrounding Articles are State-law-enabling clauses.

The three six-month deadlines (audit under 243ZM(4), annual general body meeting under 243ZN, and returns filing under 243ZP) form a coordinated annual compliance cycle for every co-operative society.
breakdown.how_to_read: Read Article 243ZP as the compliance-reporting capstone of the Article 243ZM/243ZN/243ZO trio — together these four Articles create a complete, self-reinforcing annual financial-accountability and member-transparency cycle for every co-operative society, all keyed to the same six-month post-financial-year benchmark.

sections.title: Offences and penalties
key_terms: five mandatory minimum offence categories for co-operative society State penal law
authorised person under Article 243ZQ

breakdown.plain_summary: Article 243ZQ empowers State law to create offences and penalties relating to co-operative societies, but does not leave the offence list entirely to State discretion — clause (2) mandates that five specific categories of wrongdoing (false returns/information, disobedience of lawful orders, employer's failure to remit deducted employee contributions within fourteen days, an officer/custodian's wilful failure to hand over society property to an authorised person, and electoral corrupt practices) must be included as offences in every State's co-operative penal law.
essential_elements: Clause (1) is the general enabling power: State law may create co-operative-related offences and penalties.

Clause (2) converts that general power into a floor of mandatory content — the five listed act/omission categories must be criminalised, though States remain free to add further offences beyond this floor.
Item (a) covers false returns/information and wilful non-furnishing of required information.
Item (b) covers wilful or unexcused disobedience of lawful summons/requisitions/written orders under the State Act.
Item (c) covers an employer's failure to remit employee-deducted amounts to the society within fourteen days.
Item (d) covers an officer/custodian's wilful failure to hand over society property to an 'authorised person' (the Article 243ZH(a) defined term, elaborated by this Article's own context).
Item (e) covers corrupt practices at any stage of board/office-bearer elections.
exceptions_and_qualifications: This mandatory-minimum-offence-list drafting technique is unusual for the Constitution generally — most enabling clauses across Parts IX, IXA, and IXB simply permit State legislation without dictating specific content, whereas Article 243ZQ(2) constitutionally guarantees a penal floor to deter specific historically identified abuses (falsified returns, defiance of regulatory authority, misappropriated employee deductions, property retention by outgoing officers, and election-rigging).

Item (c)'s fourteen-day employer-remittance rule closely resembles employee-provident-fund-style deduction-and-remittance obligations, reflecting a specific concern about employers withholding co-operative-society deductions (e.g., thrift/credit society contributions deducted from salary) from members' accounts.

Item (e)'s corrupt-practices offence directly reinforces the Article 243ZK election-timing and Article 243ZJ board-composition guarantees by criminalising conduct that would undermine genuinely free co-operative elections.
breakdown.how_to_read: Read Article 243ZQ's clause (2) list as a constitutional floor, not a ceiling — States must criminalise at least these five categories, but nothing prevents broader State penal schemes for co-operative societies.

sections.title: Application to multi-State co-operative societies
sections.raw_text: 243ZR.
